reconcile.note: Keil & Delitzsch explain that Caleb alone is named because he spoke first, even though Joshua stood beside him and later joined the appeal to the people.

discrepancy.note: Wellhausen treats the single-spy JE and dual-spy Priestly strands of Numbers 13-14 as a source doublet, of which this Caleb-alone vs Caleb-and-Joshua divergence is one case.

quotes.text: The spies are sent out according to the Jehovist from Kadesh, according to the Priestly Code from the wilderness of Paran… In the former Caleb is the only good spy, in the latter Caleb and Joshua.
quotes.attr: Julius Wellhausen (d. 1918), Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1885), on the Jehovist/Priestly doublet in the spies narrative of Numbers 13-14.

quotes.text: Caleb is one of the spies, but not Joshua.
quotes.attr: Julius Wellhausen (d. 1918), Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1885), on Deuteronomy's use of the single-spy Jehovist strand of the spies narrative.

sides.snippet: Caleb stilled the people before Moses, and said, Let us go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it.
sides.verseText: Caleb stilled the people before Moses, and said, Let us go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it.
